trend.title: U.S. office vacancy eases to 19.8% in Q3 2026, but Class B and C vacancy keeps rising (Cushman & Wakefield)
trend.scope: U.S. office market, 92 markets tracked by Cushman & Wakefield, Q3 2026 Office MarketBeat
trend.metric: 19.8% national vacancy (down 25 bps year over year, from a 20.1% high in Q3 2025); +50,000 sf Q3 net absorption; 7.1 msf delivered year to date
trend.summary: Cushman & Wakefield put national office vacancy at 19.8% at the end of the third quarter, 25 basis points lower than a year earlier and down from the recent 20.1% high reached in Q3 2025. Net absorption was only slightly positive at 50,000 square feet, but it was the fifth straight quarter of gains, and vacancy fell year over year in 48 of the 92 markets the firm tracks. The improvement is concentrated at the top: vacancy in top-tier buildings has dropped 215 basis points over two years while Class B and C vacancy continues to climb. New supply remains thin, with just 7.1 msf delivered in the first three quarters of 2026.
trend.significance: A national vacancy rate still near one in five, with the gap between trophy and commodity buildings widening, means owners of older Class B and C office stock face falling rents and values that strain debt-service and loan-to-value covenants at refinancing. Tenants in those buildings gain leverage in renewals, co-tenancy and abatement disputes, while lenders on lower-tier assets should expect more modification requests, receiverships and deed-in-lieu negotiations even as the headline number improves.

verification.claim: National office vacancy 19.8% at close of Q3, down 25 bps year over year, third consecutive quarter of improvement
verification.quote: National office vacancy stood at 19.8% at the close of Q3. While vacancy has remained broadly stable near 20% for the past two years, it declined 25 basis points (bps) from a year ago, marking the third consecutive quarter of year-over-year improvement.
Sublease availability reached its most recent peak in Q1 2024, while national vacancy reached a recent high of 20.1% in Q3 2025 and has since declined to 19.8%.

verification.claim: Net absorption +50,000 sf in Q3, fifth consecutive positive quarter
verification.quote: Net absorption totaled positive 50,000 square feet (sf) during the third quarter, extending the market’s streak of positive absorption to five consecutive quarters.

verification.claim: Vacancy lower year over year in 48 of 92 tracked markets
verification.quote: Vacancy was also lower than a year ago in 48 of the 92 U.S. markets tracked by Cushman & Wakefield, including San Francisco, Manhattan, Orange County, Charlotte, Phoenix and Dallas.

verification.claim: Top-tier vacancy down 215 bps over two years; Class B and C vacancy still rising
verification.quote: Vacancy among top-tier office properties has declined 215 bps over the past two years, while vacancy in Class B and C properties has continued to rise, highlighting the widening performance gap between higher-quality buildings and the broader market.

verification.claim: 7.1 msf delivered in first three quarters of 2026
verification.quote: Just 7.1 msf of new office space was delivered through the first three quarters of 2026, approximately one-fifth of the historical average.

verification.claim: Report is the Q3 2026 U.S. Office MarketBeat
verification.quote: Cushman & Wakefield (NYSE: CWK), a leading global commercial real estate services firm, announced today that its Q3 2026 U.S. Office MarketBeat  shows continued momentum in the U.S. office market, with national vacancy declining year-over-year for the third consecutive quarter, sublease availability falling to its lowest level since 2020 and new construction remaining near historic lows.
